(BY SHRI RITU RAJ BHATNAGAR, ADVOCATE)
 AND  THE STATE OF MADHYA PRADESH STATION HOUSE  OFFICER THROUGH POLICE STATION PIPLODA,
 DISTRICT RATLAM (MADHYA PRADESH)
 
 (BY SHRI KAPIL MAHANT, G.A.)
 This application coming on for admission this day, the   following:
 ORDER They are heard.

sentences.text: Perused the case diary / challan papers.

This is the first bail application filed by the applicant under Section 439 of Criminal Procedure Code, 1973, as he / she is implicated in connection with Crime No.380/2022 registered at Police Station Piploda, District Ratlam (MP) for offence punishable under Section 419, 420, 467, 468, 471, 120(B) of Indian Penal Code, 1860 and Section 82(A)(B)(C) of Registration Act.
The applicant is in custody since 15/12/2023.
The allegation against the applicant is that he was also involved i the aforesaid case wherein a conspiracy was hatched to sell the land by impersonation.

Counsel for the applicant has submitted that the co-accused in the present caseMubarik Kha has already been granted anticipatory bail by this Court in M.Cr.C. No.61012/2023/2023 vide order dated 04/01/2023 and the case of the present applicant is akin to that of co-accused Mubarik.

It is further submitted that the applicant is lodged in jail since 15/12/2023 and the final conclusion of the Amjad vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 16 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/134546623/
1 trial is likely to take sufficient long time.

entities.text: Amjad vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence, it is submitted that the bail application be allowed and he be released on bail on the ground of parity.

Counsel for the respondent / State, on the other hand has opposed the prayer and it is submitted that no case for grant of bail is made out.
Having considered the rival submissions and on perusal of the case diary as also the order passed by this Court in the case of co-accused, this Court finds force with the contentions raised by learned counsel for the applicant and further taking note of the fact that the final conclusion of the trial is likely to take sufficient long time, in the considered opinion of this Court, the applicant's application deserves to be allowed.
Accordingly, without commenting on the merits of the case, the application filed by the applicant is allowed.

The applicant is directed to be released on bail upon furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.25,000/- (rupees twenty five thousand) with one solvent surety of the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court for his/her regular appearance before the trial Court during trial with a condition that he / she shall remain present before the court concerned during trial and shall also abide by the conditions enumerated under Section 437 (3) Criminal Procedure Code, 1973.
Certified copy as per rules.

(SUBODH ABHYANKAR) JUDGE krjoshi Amjad vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 16 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/134546623/
